title: Advisor
summary: Asks a stronger model for an outside verdict on scope and direction, before you commit to a plan.

explain.what: The advisor skill brings in an outside consultant: the model in your advisor role (or its second opinion, or both). It reads a short brief and the files that matter and says whether the plan is right-sized, what to change or cut, and only the questions a human really has to decide.
explain.does: Day to day you say /advisor at a scope-shaping moment. Your agent writes the brief and asks the advisor through ask-model, which checks that the model asked for is the one that answered (where its CLI reports one). The advisor may read files and run commands to check its points, but it must not change anything: if a file changes anyway, you are told which ones, and nothing is reverted. Your agent checks the advisor's points against the code and shows you the verdict with its own agreement or disagreement. ask-model comes with model-id (acs install-model-id); the pack will not install until both are on your PATH.
changes: ~/.claude/skills/advisor/ and ~/.codex/skills/advisor/ (the skill and its contract, for the CLIs you have)
~/.agent-config-studio/roles.json, only for the advisor role you choose at install if not set yet (no model is set for you; kept after uninstall)
explain.undo: Uninstalling removes the skill folders. A file you edited after installing is kept and reported.

variants.label: Both
variants.hint: /advisor both — the two, blind, in parallel

steps.label: Brief
steps.what: The goal, the constraints and the call to make.

steps.label: Advise
steps.what: A scope verdict and its reasons, read-only.

both.what: Both answer blind; you see where they agree and split.

steps.label: Bring it back
steps.what: Checks it against the repo; asks you only what it cannot settle.

changes: ~/.claude/skills/advisor/SKILL.md and advisor-contract.md (Claude Code; Grok reads this folder too)
